change: Default x86-64 emission considers functions with raw memory, floating-point arithmetic and at most 400 IR instructions for the existing vectorizer. Only loops with no bounds checks to version qualify. The original overlap guard, SSE2/AVX2 selection and scalar remainder remain; debug/watch/REPL and non-x86 targets retain their prior paths.
validation: 4933 passed in 166.76s with two test workers, following independent three-generation C bootstrap. Focused 289 passed in 13.61s; new pointer alias and parallel checks 28 passed in 5.70s. Ruff and git diff --check passed.
coverage: Default/release native/web, float32/float64, explicit SSE2 fallback also in default builds
Disjoint, exactly aliased and overlapping pointer loops for lengths 0 through 19; original values remain independent on COW updates
Ordered floating-point reduction remains scalar: [1e16, 1, -1e16, 2] sums to 2 in the explicit loop
Full language, game/network, editor, debugger, watch, packaging, upstream and development-driver gate
decision: Keep: about 29% less elapsed time for the default matrix workload, with paired compilation CPU changes around -1% to +0.6%. Broad application results range from approximately neutral to 2.3% slower; no broad application speedup claim.
limits: Native matrix wall time with CPUs 2/3 and one/two threads; thread CPU application timings on CPU 2. Seven paired samples each for matrix/compilation/apps.

Rendering was a short three-pair validation run (nine fixed simulation frames per process), with substantial host noise. Forest/Dunes PNGs matched exactly and were visually inspected; no game-frame speedup claimed.
Default matrix remains about 2.10x the serial C kernel time. Release remains a separate broader optimization pipeline.
Comments in the compiler were clarified after the full gate; executable code is unchanged. Benchmark render now accepts --mode default while retaining release as its default.
